findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), each with its "Best hostels" line and chevron
findings.fault: The cards look like links, but none of them goes anywhere. Each is a white raised card with a heavy shadow and a strong edge. It has a :hover rule and a "Best hostels" line in the link colour with a chevron. The parts map shows all three as static, so tapping a card does nothing. The page is meant to send visitors to the destination guides, and this is the only place it offers them. "Explore destinations" and the nav's "Destinations" both lead here, so the guides can't be reached from the homepage at all.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next stop in Bali or Lombok. They follow "Explore destinations", tap Canggu to see its best hostels, and nothing happens. The page fails one of its three jobs. A brand that sells trust also looks broken on first visit.

findings.where: Nav "How we rank"; footer "How we rank", "Privacy", "Terms" and "Report content"
findings.fault: Every one of these links points back to this same page. Each looks like a working link (underlined, in the nav or footer) and promises a page of its own, but clicking it just reloads or scrolls the homepage. The privacy policy is unreachable on a page that asks visitors to hand over their email address.
findings.who_objects: A traveller who wants to know how Manta ranks hostels on merit before trusting it. The page's own pitch rests on that claim, and the link proves nothing. The same goes for a visitor checking the privacy policy before signing up, and a hostel owner looking for terms or a way to report content. Each finds nothing, which undercuts the honesty the product is built on.

findings.where: Hero: the coral "Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news" button
findings.fault: The page's main action, collecting launch-news contacts, is only a mailto link. Signing up means leaving the page for a mail app and writing an email with no idea what to say. Nothing confirms the visitor is on a list. On a desktop with no mail app set up, the click does nothing they can see.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a phone in transit who wants launch news. They expect to type an address and tap once, but they're sent off to compose a cold email to a stranger, so many give up. The founder loses the contacts this page exists to collect.

findings.fault: The two nav links have the same function but look different. "How we rank" is underlined and "Destinations" is not. A visitor can't tell whether the underline marks the current page or a different kind of link, or whether "Destinations" is a link at all.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning the nav. One look should mean one thing. Here the difference suggests a state (current page or selected) that isn't real, which makes the nav harder to read at a glance.
